question: does prepending a ~50-100 token LLM situating prefix to each seeded session unit (Anthropic contextual retrieval, write-time) lift retrieval on our stack?
design: paired 20-question probe (LongMemEval-S, seed 17); both arms seed session-unit documents (v4+ granularity, date-threaded); the ctx arm's units are prefixed by glm-5.3-flash situating summaries generated at write time (846 sessions, ~5 rejected by the provider's content filter and degraded to no-prefix). Metric: session-level gold-evidence recall@8, plain orchestrated-off retrieval, no answerer.
findings: No detectable gain on this stack: the strong existing baseline (hybrid lexical+semantic retrieval over session units with date threading) already sits at 0.85 recall@8, and the prefix moves nothing net.

Consistent with the independent ECIR replication of contextual retrieval (+0.005-0.012 nDCG under strong embedders) rather than the vendor's -49% failure-rate claim; our baseline is precisely the strong-embedder regime where the effect fades.
Probe verdict: write-time contextual prefixes do NOT enter the product - the per-write LLM cost buys no recall here.
honest_reading: n=20 gives roughly +/-16pp CI, so the precise claim is 'no gain detected', not 'provably zero'; the unrecovered 15% are hard vocabulary-gap questions where a situating prefix plausibly cannot help. Provider content-filter rejections (~5/846) and injection-guard false positives during seeding affected both arms identically (same seeded texts).
